title: Support Vector Machines: Transforming Non-Linear Data for Linear Separation

cues.en: -: Hello and welcome back to the course on machine learning.
cues.zh: 你好，歡迎回到機器學習課程。

cues.en: In today's tutorial, we will find out how we can take our non-linearly separable data set, map it to our higher dimension and get a linearly separable data set,
cues.zh: 今天要了解如何把非線性可分的資料集映射到更高維度，得到線性可分的資料集，

cues.en: invoke the support vector machine algorithm, build a decision boundary for our data set, and then project all of that back into our original dimensions.
cues.zh: 再使用支援向量機演算法，為資料集建立決策邊界，最後把這些投影回原本的維度。

cues.en: So, quite a lot to cover. Let's get started.
cues.zh: 要講的內容不少，開始吧。

cues.en: First off, we're going to look at a simplified example.
cues.zh: 首先看一個簡化的例子。

cues.en: We're going to look at a one-dimensional data set.
cues.zh: 我們看一維資料集。

cues.en: So, normally we visualize everything in the PowerPoint with two dimensions to make it, you know, look pretty and so that we can kind of understand
cues.zh: 通常投影片都用二維呈現，讓畫面好看，也讓我們能理解

cues.en: how it would work in multiple dimensions, but, right now, that will be a bit too complex for us to start with so we're going to start with a single dimension.
cues.zh: 多維情況會如何運作。不過現在一開始那樣有點複雜，所以從一維開始。

cues.en: So, here we've got the X one-dimension, we've got some points here, so we've got nine data points, and as we can see they are non-linearly separable.
cues.zh: 這裡是 X 這一個維度，有一些點，共九個資料點，可以看到它們不是線性可分的。

cues.en: So, in a, in this dimensional in a single dimension, dimensional space a linear separator would not be a line it would be a dot, right?
cues.zh: 在這個一維空間中，線性分隔物不是直線，而是一個點，對吧？

cues.en: So in a two dimensional space, a linear separator is a line, in a three-dimensional space it's a hyperplane,
cues.zh: 二維空間的線性分隔物是直線，三維空間則是超平面，

cues.en: but in a one-dimensional space it's a single dot.
cues.zh: 但一維空間中就是單一的點。

cues.en: So can we separate separate the green from the red with a single dot here?
cues.zh: 這裡能用一個點把綠色與紅色分開嗎？

cues.en: No, we cannot.
cues.zh: 不行。

cues.en: We, if we put it here, then these will be separated from that.
cues.zh: 放在這裡，只能把這些與那個分開。

cues.en: If we put it here it'll be separated from that.
cues.zh: 放在這裡，又只能把這些與那個分開。

cues.en: So, this is a non-linearly separable data set.
cues.zh: 所以這是一個非線性可分的資料集。

cues.en: Now, how can we apply the method of increasing the dimensionality of this space to make it a linearly separable data set in a higher dimension?
cues.zh: 現在要如何增加這個空間的維度，讓資料集在更高維度中成為線性可分呢？

cues.en: That's what we're going to look at.
cues.zh: 這就是要看的內容。

cues.en: And it might seem impossible, right?
cues.zh: 聽起來可能不可能，對吧？

cues.en: So the first time I learned about this, for me it was like, wow, how can you take a non-linearly separable data set and somehow magically increase the dimensionality
cues.zh: 第一次學到這個時，我心想，哇，怎麼可能把非線性可分的資料集，像變魔術一樣增加維度，

cues.en: and you get a linearly separable data set?
cues.zh: 就得到線性可分的資料集？

cues.en: That, you know, sounded, like, absurd.
cues.zh: 聽起來很荒謬。

cues.en: But it is actually possible and that's what we're going to see right now.
cues.zh: 但確實做得到，我們現在就會看到。

cues.en: So, we're going to create this mapping function on the fly.
cues.zh: 我們要現場建立這個映射函數。

cues.en: So, let's say that this point over here is around 5.
cues.zh: 假設這裡這個點大約是 5。

cues.en: So this is 0 over here and then somewhere here we've got 5.
cues.zh: 這裡是 0，這附近則是 5。

cues.en: It doesn't really matter, it can be any number, but just for argument sake, let's say that this point over here is 5, right?
cues.zh: 數字其實不重要，任何數字都可以，只是為了說明，假設這裡的點是 5。

cues.en: And then it keeps going.
cues.zh: 然後繼續延伸。

cues.en: So, our first step to build the mapping function.
cues.zh: 建立映射函數的第一步。

cues.en: There can be multiple mapping functions that you can build, I'm just gonna show you one that came to my mind.
cues.zh: 可以建立很多不同映射函數，我只是示範一個想到的例子。

cues.en: So, the first step will be to go F = X-5 so to subtract 5 from our data set and that is going to, what is that going to do?
cues.zh: 第一步設 F = X - 5，也就是把資料集減去 5。這會產生什麼效果？

cues.en: That is going to move everything to the left.
cues.zh: 會把一切往左移。

cues.en: So, basically, now this is what the result looks like.
cues.zh: 所以結果基本上就像這樣。

cues.en: So if you take 5, you subtract 5 from X, you'll get, you know, like these ones will go into negative, these ones will stay in positive.
cues.zh: 從 X 減去 5，這些值會變成負數，這些則維持正數。

cues.en: And then the next step would be to square all of that.
cues.zh: 下一步是把它全部平方。

cues.en: So F is now = to X-5 squared.
cues.zh: 現在 F = (X - 5)²。

cues.en: So how will that all look like?
cues.zh: 這樣會長什麼樣子？

cues.en: Well, basically, you'll have this squared function going through your chart and then all of these will be projected
cues.zh: 基本上，圖中會有這個平方函數，所有這些點會投影

cues.en: onto the function.
cues.zh: 到這個函數上。

cues.en: There we go.
cues.zh: 好了。

cues.en: So, that's what it looks like F = X-5 squared.
cues.zh: 這就是 F = (X - 5)² 的樣子。

cues.en: And now what we want to do is we just want to see that it is, indeed, linearly separable.
cues.zh: 現在要看它是否確實線性可分。

cues.en: So there we go.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.en: There's our linear separator.
cues.zh: 這就是線性分隔線。

cues.en: So, in a two-dimensional space, as we remember, a linear separator is a straight line, and, as you can see, this data set became linearly separable
cues.zh: 記得二維空間中的線性分隔線是直線。可以看到，資料集在這個維度中

cues.en: in this dimension.
cues.zh: 變成線性可分了。

cues.en: I know it's, it's surprising and even a bit shocking but, indeed, it is the case.
cues.zh: 我知道很令人驚訝，甚至有點震撼，但確實如此。

cues.en: So, you can see that we were able to take this line and separate all of the red elements or of our data set from the green element
cues.zh: 可以看到，我們用這條線把資料集中所有紅色元素與綠色元素分開，

cues.en: and that's it.
cues.zh: 就這樣。

cues.en: And, then, what we would do next from here is we would project everything back onto our original space and we would know how
cues.zh: 接下來會把所有東西投影回原始空間，就知道如何

cues.en: to functionally separate the green from the red.
cues.zh: 用函數把綠色與紅色分開。

cues.en: And that is what happens when you map something to a higher dimension.
cues.zh: 這就是映射到更高維度時會發生的事。

cues.en: So, now, knowing this example and seeing that it works in reality, we can proceed to a higher dimension, you know, to start with a two-dimensional space.
cues.zh: 現在理解這個例子，也看到它確實有效，就能從更高維度開始，例如二維空間。

cues.en: So, let's have a look.
cues.zh: 來看看。

cues.en: So, there's our two-dimensional space and, basically, you would apply the same principle.
cues.zh: 這是二維空間，基本上套用相同原則。

cues.en: So, here you cannot apply, or you cannot invoke, the support vector machine algorithm because it is not a non-linearly separable data set
cues.zh: 這裡無法直接使用支援向量機演算法，因為在這個空間中，資料集並不是線性可分的，

cues.en: in this space, but, then, you would apply some sort of mapping function.
cues.zh: 但可以套用某種映射函數。

cues.en: Like, right now, we won't go into detail what exactly mapping function it would be, and, again, they could be multiple different options and so on.
cues.zh: 現在不深入討論具體使用哪個映射函數，同樣可能有很多不同選項。

cues.en: But, basically, based on the previous example, we now know that it's possible, like, we've seen empirical evidence that it is possible to do.
cues.zh: 但根據前面的例子，現在知道這是可能的，我們已經看過可以做到的實際證據。

cues.en: And the same thing applies to two-dimensional space moving into a three-dimensional space.
cues.zh: 從二維空間到三維空間也適用相同概念。

cues.en: You would map it into a three-dimensional space and then, somehow, it would become a linearly separable data set in this space.
cues.zh: 把它映射到三維空間，就能以某種方式在這個空間中成為線性可分資料集。

cues.en: And here we've got the new dimension, which is Z, and in a three-dimensional space the linear separator is no longer aligned; it's a hyperplane.
cues.zh: 這裡的新維度是 Z。在三維空間，線性分隔物不再是直線，而是超平面。

cues.en: And so this hyperplane separates the two parts of our data set in the way we want.
cues.zh: 這個超平面以我們想要的方式分開資料集的兩個部分。

cues.en: So, the support vector machine algorithm has helped us build this hyperplane.
cues.zh: 支援向量機演算法幫我們建立了這個超平面。

cues.en: And then, basically, so we've got this result, then we just project it back into our two-dimensional space and we've got this circle that encompasses our classes,
cues.zh: 得到結果後，再投影回二維空間，就會得到這個包住類別，

cues.en: or separates our classes.
cues.zh: 或分開類別的圓。

cues.en: And there we go, we've got the non-linear separator.
cues.zh: 好了，這就是非線性分隔線。

cues.en: So, as you can see, we can still, even though we have got a a bit of a more complex problem where we cannot directly
cues.zh: 可以看到，雖然問題稍微複雜，無法像以前一樣直接

cues.en: apply the support vector machine algorithm as we used to, we can still go into a higher dimension and then apply the support vector machine algorithm.
cues.zh: 套用支援向量機演算法，但仍能先進入更高維度，再使用支援向量機演算法。

cues.en: And, like, we won't go into detail if it's possible all the time, and if there's cases when it's not possible, and so on what you would do there, but the point is that
cues.zh: 我們不深入討論是否每次都行、有沒有不行的情況，以及那時該怎麼做。重點是，

cues.en: there is a solution that you can explore the higher dimensions so that this is not a dead end.
cues.zh: 可以探索更高維度來尋找解法，所以並非走投無路。

cues.en: You can just do that. But there's a problem.
cues.zh: 可以這麼做，但有一個問題。

cues.en: There's a problem with this algorithm.
cues.zh: 這個演算法有個問題。

cues.en: And the problem is that mapping to a higher dimensional space can be highly compute-intensive so it might require a lot of computation, a lot of processing power,
cues.zh: 映射到更高維空間可能需要大量運算，也就是很多計算與處理能力，

cues.en: and, you know, the larger your data set the more of a problem this can cause.
cues.zh: 資料集越大，這個問題可能越嚴重。

cues.en: And, therefore, this approach isn't the best because you can imagine, like, you have a a data set and then mapping it to a higher dimension,
cues.zh: 因此這不是最佳方法。可以想像，先把資料集映射到更高維度，

cues.en: performing all the calculations there, and then coming back to your lower dimension.
cues.zh: 在那裡進行所有計算，再回到較低維度。

cues.en: That can, even for a computer, not just, like, in our minds as as humans, but just, like, for a computer that can cause a lot
cues.zh: 不只是人類腦中難以處理，就連電腦也可能因此出現大量

cues.en: of delays.
cues.zh: 延遲。

cues.en: It can cause a lot of, like, processing backlog and issues in, in that sense.
cues.zh: 也可能累積很多待處理運算，出現相關問題。

cues.en: And we don't want that to happen, and, therefore, we are going to explore something else.
cues.zh: 我們不希望如此，因此要探索其他方式。

cues.en: We're gonna explore a different approach which is called, in mathematics, the kernel trick.
cues.zh: 我們要研究另一種方法，數學上叫做核心技巧。

cues.en: And that approach is going to help us perform very similar, gets very similar results,
cues.zh: 這個方法可以得到非常相似的結果，

cues.en: but without having to go to a higher dimensional space.
cues.zh: 卻不需要實際進入更高維空間。

cues.en: And we're going to talk about that in the next tutorial.
cues.zh: 下一堂會談這個。

cues.en: It's gonna be exciting and I can't wait to see you there.
cues.zh: 會很精彩，迫不及待要在那裡見到你。

cues.en: Until then, happy analyzing.
cues.zh: 在此之前，分析愉快。
